title: Assessment of the brooks pope and marcoline (BPM) airfoil noise prediction model
author: Afonso André Ribeiro
abstract: The intense occupation of the urban areas impact in the resources consumptions and pollutions emissions. In the e?ort to reduce the impact due to the power generation, renewable sources was preferred instead of mineral sources. But even renewable sources have some type of pollution like the noise emitted by wind turbine. As consequence of this noise, many countries created regulations specifying criteria to install the turbines. Other important emitter of noise pollution is the aircrafts that ?y over big cities in low altitude. Similarly to wind turbines the government start to regulate the noise emitted by planes. For this reasons companies in the related areas gave more attention to the topic requiring from the universities models to predict noise generation and research facilities capable to test their products. On that way, ensure that the aeroacustic wind tunnel of the University of Twente is able to acquire reliable data for the study of aeroacustic is very relevant. Two main experiments for the theme will be performed. First is the measurements of boundary layer, utilizing hot-wire anemometry combined with a troverse system. The results showed a strong correspondence between the acquired data and compared one. Second aims to measure the noise generated exclusively by an airfoil isolated by the background noise. It was possible detect agreement between the simulation and acquired data also de?ne the equipment limitations. Thus the tunnel is enabled to perform acoustic aeroacustics experiments respecting it limitations.
